definitions.name: Paper-independent bounded-build certified complex contour arithmetic substrate
definitions.construction:
The paper-independent bounded-build obligation \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) is the following finite implementation specification.  A certified real record consists of rational closed intervals \(I_m=[I_m^-,I_m^+]\), an executable modulus \(\mu:\mathbb Q_{>0}\to\mathbb N\), and the semantic contract
\[
 x\in I_{m+1}\subseteq I_m,
 \qquad
 I_{\mu(e)}^+-I_{\mu(e)}^-\le e.
\]
A positive record additionally supplies a rational \(p>0\) with \(p\le x\).  Executable code may inspect only the interval, modulus, and positivity fields.  It may not inspect a semantic exact-real value.

For rational intervals \(A=[a_-,a_+]\) and \(B=[b_-,b_+]\), define
\[
 A+B=[a_-+b_-,a_++b_+],
 \qquad
 A-B=[a_--b_+,a_+-b_-],
\]
\[
 A B=
 [\min\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\},
  \max\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\}].
\]
A complex rectangle is \(A+iB\).  Complex addition, subtraction, conjugation, and multiplication are implemented by these endpoint operations and
\[
 (A+iB)(C+iD)=(AC-BD)+i(AD+BC).
\]
For \(A=[a_-,a_+]\), put
\[
 \operatorname{sq}_{-}(A)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&a_-\le0\le a_+,\\
 \min\{a_-^2,a_+^2\},&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \operatorname{sq}_{+}(A)=\max\{a_-^2,a_+^2\}.
\]
Thus \(|A+iB|^2\) is enclosed by the rational interval obtained by adding the corresponding square bounds.  Rational bisection between nonnegative rational endpoints gives lower and upper square-root enclosures: after \(q\) bisections their width is at most the initial width times \(2^{-q}\).  This supplies certified modulus lower and upper bounds.  Division is the guarded operation
\[
 \frac{A+iB}{C+iD}
 =(A+iB)(C-iD)(C^2+D^2)^{-1},
\]
and is executed only when the modulus routine has returned a rational lower bound \(m>0\); outward division by the positive rational interval enclosing \(C^2+D^2\) is then sound.

The certified name of \(\pi\) is constructed, rather than postulated, from Machin's identity
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239).
\]
For \(0<x<1\), the first \(N+1\) terms of
\[
 \arctan x=\sum_{j=0}^{N}(-1)^j\frac{x^{2j+1}}{2j+1}+R_N(x),
 \qquad
 |R_N(x)|\le\frac{x^{2N+3}}{2N+3},
\]
give rational nested enclosures after intersecting the first \(m+1\) requested enclosures.  If \(e=p/q>0\) is in lowest terms, the explicit choice \(N=5q+5\) makes the propagated Machin remainder smaller than \(e\), so this is an effective modulus with finite fuel.

For a rational interval contained in \([-B,B]\), with rational \(B\ge0\), evaluate the Taylor polynomials for \(\exp\), \(\sin\), and \(\cos\) by the preceding interval operations.  The Lagrange remainders are bounded respectively by
\[
 3^{\lceil B\rceil}\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.
\]
For a requested rational error \(e=p/q>0\), take
\[
 N=\lceil2B\rceil+q+2\lceil B\rceil+2.
\]
After the index \(\lceil2B\rceil\), successive absolute Taylor terms decrease by at least a factor \(1/2\); since \(3^{\lceil B\rceil}<2^{2\lceil B\rceil}\) and \(2^{-q}\le q^{-1}\le e\), this displayed \(N\) gives a sound error at most \(e\).  Finite intersections make the output rectangles nested.  Hence
\[
 \exp(x+iy)=\exp(x)\{\cos y+i\sin y\}
\]
has a nested complex-rectangle extension with an effective modulus on every bounded input rectangle.  Combining the constructed \(\pi\) name with these trigonometric operations gives, from a positive radius record \(\mathfrak r\) and integers \(N\ge1\), \(0\le q<N\), certified circle-node records for
\[
 r\exp(2\pi iq/N)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 2\pi i r\exp(2\pi iq/N).
\]

Finite rectangle sums and products are primitive recursive.  If a complex-valued function on \([0,1]\) has a supplied rational Lipschitz bound \(L\), a uniform mesh with
\[
 N_{\mathrm{mesh}}=\lceil L/e\rceil+1
\]
has oscillation at most \(e\) on each cell.  Evaluating every node to a rational error budget divided by the displayed finite number of operations therefore yields sound finite infimum, supremum, and trapezoidal-integral enclosures.  Their fuel consists of \(N_{\mathrm{mesh}}+1\) node calls, the displayed Taylor cutoffs, square-root bisection cutoffs, and a finite number of endpoint operations.  Absolute value of a real interval is implemented by the square-free endpoint rule implicit in \(\operatorname{sq}_{-}\) and \(\operatorname{sq}_{+}\), and has the same compositional modulus property.

A concrete implementation discharges \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) only if it implements these algorithms, exports their soundness and effective-modulus contracts, and compiles the resulting module.  This definition is the explicit bounded-build obligation; it does not state or imply that the missing complex operations are already exported by Causalean.  Until such an implementation is added and compiled, later executable conclusions are conditional on a build satisfying this specification.

definitions.name: Certified translated-dyadic contour bank
definitions.construction:
Let \(\operatorname{Name}_{+}(x)\) denote an actually supplied positive certified-real record satisfying \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\).  As part of the experiment convention, fix once for all the single actual record
\[
 \mathfrak p_{\star}=
 \bigl(k,\mathfrak d_{\star},\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star},
       \mathfrak r_{0,\star},\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(k\) is exact and
\[
 \mathfrak d_{\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\delta),\quad
 \mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\psi_{\eta}),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{0,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_0),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{1,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_1),
\]
with the value contracts
\[
 k=r+1,\qquad
 R_0=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
       (\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)},
 \qquad R_1=R_0+1.
\]
Each positive name includes its rational positivity witness.  The record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) is fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies, and it is the only primitive record used by both the bank and the estimator.  The construction reads only its supplied interval, modulus, and positivity fields.  It never reconstructs a name from an exact real and does not quantify over alternative records representing the same constants.

Invoke the supplied moduli of \(\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}\) and \(\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\) at error one.  If the returned intervals have rational upper endpoints \(u_{\psi}\) and \(u_R\), put
\[
 U_{\psi}=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_{\psi}\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 U_R=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_R\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^2(U_R+2)^3.
\]
Set
\[
 m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,
 \qquad d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},
 \qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad J=2^{m_{\star}-1}+1.
\]
For \(q=0,\ldots,2^{m_{\star}-1}\), use certified addition on the fixed record \(\mathfrak r_{0,\star}\) and the rational point record for \(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\) to form
\[
 \mathfrak\rho_q
 =\mathfrak r_{0,\star}+\operatorname{Name}(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}).
\]
Its value is \(\rho_q=R_0+1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\).  Enumerate these radii increasingly and set \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\).

Define the integers
\[
 e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^2(U_R+1)^2,
 \qquad
 d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}=3(2U_R+1),
\]
\[
 u_{\star}=2e_{\star}
 +N_{\mathrm{cert}}(m_{\star}+d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}),
 \qquad
 a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}}>0.
\]
Every output datum is obtained by the displayed finite modulus calls, rational endpoint operations, and primitive recursion over displayed integer bounds.  There is no unbounded search, \(\operatorname{Classical.choose}\), proof-selected \(\operatorname{Nat.find}\), exact-real inspection, or query to \(M\), \(\eta\), or its law.  Reusing the identical fixed record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) gives the same bank and certificate for every \(n\).  The universal guarantee is stated in \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).

definitions.name: Canonical certified split-sample statistic on the translated-dyadic bank
definitions.construction:
The construction has a mathematical layer and a represented-data layer, both relative to exactly the same experiment-wide primitive records.

Fix the record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) from \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and, once for all, fix one actual record
\[
 \mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(C_{\theta}).
\]
These records are fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies.  They are never replaced by different canonical names.

At the mathematical layer, for an ordinary real observation coordinate set
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Canonicalize only \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\) through these floor-dyadic records.  Run the finite rational procedure below with those observation records and with the already fixed, unchanged records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\), and take the value represented by its output record.  This defines \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) as a total map on ordinary real samples relative to the fixed full primitive record.  The canonical observation digits are part of this mathematical interpretation; they are not claimed to be Type-2 computable from an arbitrary real name at a dyadic boundary.  In particular, the ordinary interpretation does not silently substitute canonical primitive names.

At the represented-data layer, the full input record is
\[
 \mathfrak s_{\star}=
 \bigl((\mathfrak t_i,\mathfrak y_i,\mathfrak g_i)_{i=1}^n,
       \mathfrak p_{\star},\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathfrak t_i\), \(\mathfrak y_i\), and \(\mathfrak g_i\) are supplied canonical digital records for \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\).  The transducer is defined only relative to the displayed fixed primitive components; its correspondence claim does not quantify over alternative primitive records.  A transducer exists at this layer only relative to a concrete implementation that has been added and compiled with all contracts of \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\).  It reads no semantic exact-real field.

Invoke \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) on \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), and form \(\mathfrak z_i=\mathfrak t_i-\mathfrak g_i\) by certified subtraction.  At every certified circle node, use only the substrate's complex rectangle operations and nested complex-exponential extension to construct, by finite sums, enclosures of
\[
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Every node precision is obtained by applying the compositional modulus to a rational error budget.

For explicit mesh fuel, refine each observation record at error one and take the resulting rational upper magnitude bounds \(U_{Z,i}\), \(U_{Y,i}\), and \(U_{\rho,j}\).  Use \(e^x\le3^{\lceil x\rceil}\) for \(x\ge0\) and \(\pi<4\) to turn the finite empirical derivative sums into rational bounds for all functions below.  With \(z_j(t)=\rho_je^{2\pi it}\), put
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{2\pi it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(z_j(t))},
\]
and, after a positive integer \(N_j\) has been certified,
\[
 V_j(t)=
 \frac{\rho_je^{2\pi it}}{N_j}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(z_j(t))}.
\]
If a rational lower modulus certificate is \(m>0\), use
\[
 |W'_{0j}(t)|\le
 2\pi\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 |V'_j(t)|\le
 \frac{2\pi}{N_j}\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}\right].
\]
For a rational tolerance \(e>0\) and any resulting rational bound \(L\), take the mesh size \(\lceil L/e\rceil+1\), and allocate node error by the finite number of operations.  Thus every precision and mesh has displayed finite fuel.

On the pilot fold, compute for every \(j\) a sound interval of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\) enclosing \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{0,n}|\).  If its lower endpoint \(m_j\) is positive, guarded division and finite quadrature enclose
\[
 \int_0^1W_{0j}(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{0,n}(z)}\,dz
\]
in a complex rectangle whose coordinate widths are strictly below \(1/4\).  Record \(N_j\) exactly when the real interval contains a unique nonnegative integer and the imaginary interval contains zero; otherwise reject the circle.  A circle is admissible exactly when \(m_j\ge a_{\star}/2\) and \(N_j\ge1\).  Select an admissible circle having the greatest rational lower endpoint, with smallest-index tie-break, and return the certified zero name if none exists.

On the evaluation fold, compute the analogous modulus enclosure and return the certified zero name if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\).  Otherwise guarded division and finite quadrature give a rectangle of coordinate radius at most \(1/n\) enclosing
\[
 \int_0^1V_j(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{N_j2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz.
\]
Let \(y\in\mathbb Q\) be the rational midpoint of its real interval, represented by its rational point name.  Projection uses no exact comparison: certified addition, subtraction, multiplication by \(1/2\), and the interval absolute-value operation construct a certified name whose value is
\[
 \operatorname{clip}_{C_{\theta}}(y)
 =\frac{|y+C_{\theta}|-|y-C_{\theta}|}{2}
 =\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}(y).
\]
This certified-real name is the transducer output.

An execution trace is the finite list of input-modulus calls, returned precisions, Taylor and square-root cutoffs, mesh sizes, rational rectangle operations, guarded divisions, rational endpoint comparisons, fallback decisions, and the tie-break.  Identical full input records \(\mathfrak s_{\star}\), including their fixed primitive components, have identical traces and output records.  The value represented by that output is, by definition, the ordinary-sample Borel statistic evaluated with the same fixed primitive records.  No extensionality across arbitrary alternative names is asserted.  The procedure uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and has no access to the law of \(\eta\).  The represented-data transducer and its compiled computability conclusion remain conditional on completing the bounded-build obligation in \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\); the ordinary-sample Borel statistic and its statistical risk are mathematical objects independently of that build status.

statements.statement: If \(z_0\) is a zero of \(M\) of multiplicity \(\ell\), then for every real shift \(d\), \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]=0\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), this gives \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]=0\) and \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]=M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0)\); whenever this value is nonzero, \(\theta_0=E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]/E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\).
statements.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Fix a zero \(z_0\) of \(M\) having multiplicity \(\ell\).  By the definition of multiplicity,
\[
 M^{(j)}(z_0)=0\quad(0\le j<\ell),
 \qquad M^{(\ell)}(z_0)\ne0.
\]
All differentiations under the expectation below are legitimate: membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(\text{ass:eta-subgaussian}\), incorporated in \(\text{def:non-gaussian-class}\), give exponential moments of \(\eta\) of every real order, while \(|D_n|\le 2C_g\).  Hence every polynomial times each complex exponential appearing below is integrable, uniformly on compact subsets of the complex plane.

For an arbitrary real number \(d\), the binomial identity and the derivative formula \(M^{(j)}(z)=E_P[\eta^j e^{z\eta}]\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]
 &=E_P[(\eta+d)^{\ell-1}e^{z_0(\eta+d)}]\\
 &=e^{z_0d}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
   {\ell-1\choose j}d^{\ell-1-j}E_P[\eta^j e^{z_0\eta}]\\
 &=e^{z_0d}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
   {\ell-1\choose j}d^{\ell-1-j}M^{(j)}(z_0)=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the shift-annihilation identity.

Now fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  By \(\text{ass:independent-treatment-noise}\), the conditional law of \(\eta\) given \(X\) equals its marginal law.  Since \(D_n=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\) is \(\sigma(X)\)-measurable and real-valued, the preceding identity, applied conditionally with \(d=D_n\), yields
\[
 E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]
 =E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+D_n)\mid X]=0
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

Independence also gives the exact transform factorization
\[
 E_P[e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P[e^{z(\eta+D_n)}]=M(z)H_n(z).
\]
Differentiating this identity \(\ell\) times at \(z_0\), using the product rule and the multiplicity equalities above, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
 &=E_P[Z_n^{\ell}e^{z_0Z_n}]\\
 &=\left.\frac{d^{\ell}}{dz^{\ell}}\{M(z)H_n(z)\}\right|_{z=z_0}\\
 &=\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}{\ell\choose j}
   M^{(j)}(z_0)H_n^{(\ell-j)}(z_0)
 =M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0).
\end{aligned}
\]

Finally, by the displayed residual decomposition,
\[
 Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi.
\]
The conditional annihilation identity implies
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
 =E_P\!\left[b_n(X)E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]\right]=0.
\]
Moreover, \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), so \(J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\) is \(\sigma(X,T)\)-measurable.  The restriction \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) in \(\text{ass:outcome-mean-independence}\) therefore gives
\[
 E_P[\xi J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
 =E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\right]=0.
\]
The required products are integrable because \(b_n\) is bounded, \(\xi\) is conditionally sub-Gaussian, \(D_n\) is bounded, and \(\eta\) is sub-Gaussian.  Consequently,
\[
 E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
 =\theta_0E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)].
\]
Whenever the denominator, equivalently \(M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0)\), is nonzero, division is valid and yields
\[
 \theta_0=
 \frac{E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}
      {E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}.
\]
\end{proof}
statements.justification: This exact identity displays the global location-family null score and its relevance under residual contamination.
statements.gap: Transform-zero incompleteness is classical, but its multiplicity-adjusted score has not been used to eliminate an arbitrary PLM covariate shift created by a supplied treatment code.
statements.consumer: Known-noise implementations can estimate the causal coefficient by a single bounded or exponentially weighted moment ratio.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), \(F_n(z)=M(z)H_n(z)\) and \(G_n(z)=\theta_0F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z)\) for every \(z\in\mathbb C\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(z\in\mathbb C\).  The sub-Gaussian and boundedness conditions make every expectation and derivative below finite.  Since \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\), \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), and \(\eta\perp X\),
\[
 F_n(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}e^{zD_n}]=M(z)H_n(z).
\]
The residual equation gives \(Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi\).  Moreover \(Z_n\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), so outcome mean independence implies
\[
 E_P[\xi e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P[e^{zZ_n}E_P(\xi\mid X,T)]=0.
\]
Independence again gives
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P[e^{z\eta}]E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}]=M(z)B_n(z).
\]
Finally, differentiation under the expectation is justified by the same exponential integrability and yields \(F_n'(z)=E_P[Z_ne^{zZ_n}]\).  Substitution proves
\[
 G_n(z)=\theta_0F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z).
\]
Both identities hold for every complex \(z\).
statements.justification: The identity recovers the latent transform-zero geometry from observable learned residuals and isolates an analytic nuisance ratio.
statements.gap: Classical convolution results do not provide the outcome transform \(G_n=\theta_0F_n'+MB_n\) for a partially linear causal coefficient.
statements.consumer: The contour theorem integrates \(G_n/F_n\) and removes \(B_n/H_n\) exactly.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), let \(C_j\) be positively oriented. If \(F_n\) is zero-free on \(C_j\), \(H_n\) is zero-free on and inside \(C_j\), and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge1\), then \(\theta_0=\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)=\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}\oint_{C_j}G_n(z)/F_n(z)\,dz\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  This membership is the premise needed to invoke \(\text{lem:observable-factorization}\).  On \(C_j\), that lemma and the identity \(F_n=M H_n\) give
\[
 \frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}
 =\theta_0\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}+
   \frac{M(z)B_n(z)}{M(z)H_n(z)}
 =\theta_0\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}+\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The cancellation in the middle expression is justified pointwise on \(C_j\): by hypothesis \(F_n\) is nonzero there and \(H_n\) is nonzero there, so \(M=F_n/H_n\) is also nonzero there.  Since \(B_n\) and \(H_n\) are entire and \(H_n\) has no zero on or inside \(C_j\), the quotient \(B_n/H_n\) is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk bounded by \(C_j\).  Cauchy's theorem therefore yields
\[
 \oint_{C_j}\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}\,dz=0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Because \(F_n\) is entire and zero-free on \(C_j\), the argument principle gives
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
 \frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz=N_{C_j}(F_n).
 \tag{3}
\]
Integrating (1) and using (2)--(3) gives
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz
 =\theta_0N_{C_j}(F_n).
 \tag{4}
\]
The assumed count is a positive integer, so division by \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\) is valid.  Applying \(\text{def:contour-functional}\) to (4) proves
\[
 \theta_0
 =\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)
 =\frac{1}{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i}
   \oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz.
\]
Thus the causal target remains \(\theta_0(P)\), while the displayed observable contour ratio is its identifying functional only for a law in the stated class and under the stated boundary, zero-free, and positive-count conditions.
statements.justification: For a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), the learned-residual factorization makes the observable contour formula identify the coefficient without an outcome regression once a valid contour is given.
statements.gap: The identity requires class membership as well as the boundary zero-free, nuisance-transform zero-free, and positive-count conditions; it neither constructs nor computes the uniformly conditioned contour bank.
statements.consumer: The certified estimator fixes \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and evaluates this population identity on its selected translated-dyadic contour.

statements.statement:
With the exact Luxemburg convention in \(\text{ass:eta-subgaussian}\), set
\[
 A_k=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)},
 \qquad
 R_0=A_k(\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}.
\]
Every centered law satisfying \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta\) has a zero of \(M\) in \(\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|\le R_0\}\). Thus the zero-localization radius is the displayed numerical function of the primitive constants.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\psi=\psi_{\eta}\).  The exact Luxemburg premise gives
\[
 E_P\exp(\eta^2/\psi^2)\le2,
 \qquad E_P\eta=0.
\]
We first derive a numerical growth bound.  Let \(\eta'\) be an independent copy of \(\eta\).  If \(|t|\psi\le1\), Jensen's inequality and centering give
\[
 E_Pe^{t\eta}\le E_Pe^{t(\eta-\eta')}.
\]
The difference \(\eta-\eta'\) is symmetric.  Using \(\cosh u\le e^{u^2/2}\), \((\eta-\eta')^2\le2\eta^2+2(\eta')^2\), and then the Lyapunov inequality with exponent \(t^2\psi^2\le1\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_Pe^{t\eta}
 &\le E_P\cosh\{t(\eta-\eta')\}\\
 &\le E_P\exp\{t^2(\eta-\eta')^2/2\}\\
 &\le \{E_Pe^{t^2\eta^2}\}^2
 \le 2^{2t^2\psi^2}
 \le e^{4\psi^2t^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
If \(|t|\psi>1\), Young's inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz yield
\[
 t\eta\le\frac{\eta^2}{2\psi^2}+\frac{t^2\psi^2}{2},
 \qquad
 E_Pe^{t\eta}\le\sqrt2\,e^{t^2\psi^2/2}
 \le e^{4\psi^2t^2}.
\]
Consequently, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
 |M(z)|\le E_Pe^{\operatorname{Re}(z)\eta}
 \le \exp(4\psi^2|z|^2). \tag{1}
\]

Suppose for contradiction that \(M\) has no zero in the closed disk of radius \(R_0\).  Since \(M(0)=1\), an analytic logarithm \(f=\log M\), normalized by \(f(0)=0\), exists on a neighborhood of that disk.  Centering gives \(f'(0)=0\).  For \(0<R<R_0\), (1) gives
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R}\operatorname{Re}f(z)\le4\psi^2R^2.
\]
Apply the Carath\'eodory coefficient estimate on the radius-\(R\) disk to the positive-real-part analytic function \(4\psi^2R^2-f\).  Its value at zero is \(4\psi^2R^2\), and hence
\[
 |f^{(k)}(0)|
 \le 2k!R^{-k}\,4\psi^2R^2
 =8k!\psi^2R^{2-k}. \tag{2}
\]
Letting \(R\uparrow R_0\), using \(f^{(k)}(0)=\kappa_k(\eta)\), and invoking \(\text{ass:cumulant-separation}\), we get
\[
 \delta\le8k!\psi^2R_0^{2-k}.
\]
But the displayed definitions of \(A_k\) and \(R_0\) give
\[
 8k!\psi^2R_0^{2-k}
 =\frac{8k!}{2^{k+4}k!}\,\delta
 =2^{-k-1}\delta<\delta,
\]
a contradiction.  Thus \(M\) has a zero in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), with the asserted numerical radius.
statements.justification: The exact Luxemburg normalization yields the displayed numerical radius rather than an unspecified universal constant.
statements.gap: The result localizes a transform zero but does not by itself provide boundary conditioning.
statements.consumer: The certified translated-dyadic bank is built outside this explicit disk.

statements.statement:
Under the certified-real input convention of \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), its terminating finite searches compute, from the displayed primitive class constants and without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\), a finite translated-dyadic bank \(C_j=\{z:|z|=\rho_j\}\), \(1\le j\le J\), with \(R_0<\rho_j<R_1\), and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\). Every treatment-noise transform represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) has some \(j\) such that \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and
\[
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}.
\]
The same computed bank and certificate work uniformly in \(n\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a treatment-noise transform \(M\) represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  By \(\text{lem:zero-localization}\), it has a zero in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), so every bank circle encloses at least one zero.  The transform bound proved there gives
\[
 \log\max_{|z|=R_{\mathrm{out}}}|M(z)|
 \le4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2.
\]
Jensen's formula, with \(M(0)=1\), shows that the number of zeros strictly inside \(\{|z|<R_{\mathrm{fac}}\}\), counted with multiplicity, is at most
\[
 Q_{\star}
 =\frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
        {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}
 \le N_{\mathrm{cert}}. \tag{1}
\]
Only zeros strictly inside \(R_{\mathrm{fac}}\) are counted and factored below.

The certified translated-dyadic grid \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) is finite, lies in \((R_0,R_1)\), has more than \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}\) points, and has spacing \(d_{\star}\).  The modulus of a fixed zero can lie within \(h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3\) of at most one grid point.  Every zero capable of violating this separation at a grid radius lies strictly inside \(R_{\mathrm{fac}}\), because every grid radius is below \(R_1\) and \(R_1+h_{\star}<R_{\mathrm{fac}}\).  Hence (1) and the pigeonhole principle give a grid radius \(\rho_j\) such that
\[
 \bigl||a|-\rho_j\bigr|\ge h_{\star}
\]
for every zero \(a\) strictly inside \(R_{\mathrm{fac}}\).  This circle encloses the zero localized in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), so \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\).

Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_N\), repeated according to multiplicity, be precisely the zeros of \(M\) strictly inside \(R_{\mathrm{fac}}\), where \(N\le N_{\mathrm{cert}}\), and form the disk Blaschke product
\[
 Q(z)=\prod_{\nu=1}^N
 \frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}(z-a_\nu)}
      {R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2-\overline{a_\nu}z}.
\]
Set \(f=M/Q\), filling removable singularities.  Then \(f\) is holomorphic and zero-free on the open disk \(\{|z|<R_{\mathrm{fac}}\}\).  It may vanish on the boundary because zeros on \(|z|=R_{\mathrm{fac}}\) were deliberately not factored.  On that boundary \(|Q|=1\).  The boundary transform bound, followed by the maximum-modulus principle on smaller concentric disks and passage to the limit, gives
\[
 |f(z)|\le \exp(4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2),
 \qquad |z|<R_{\mathrm{fac}}. \tag{2}
\]
Also \(|Q(0)|\le1\) and \(M(0)=1\), so \(|f(0)|\ge1\).

Put \(A=4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\).  Since \(f\) is zero-free on the open disk, \(A-\log|f|\) is a nonnegative harmonic function there by (2), and its value at zero is at most \(A\).  The open-disk Harnack inequality therefore gives, for \(|z|\le R_1\),
\[
 A-\log|f(z)|\le\Lambda_{\star}A,
 \qquad
 |f(z)|\ge
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}. \tag{3}
\]
For \(z\in C_j\), radial separation and \(|z|\le R_1\) imply for every disk factor
\[
 \left|
 \frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}(z-a_\nu)}
      {R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2-\overline{a_\nu}z}
 \right|
 \ge \frac{|z-a_\nu|}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+|z|}
 \ge \frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}.
\]
The last base lies in \((0,1)\), and \(N\le N_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  Multiplying this bound and using (3) yields
\[
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|
 \ge
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}
 =a_{\mathrm{an}}
 \ge a_{\star}>0. \tag{4}
\]

Finally, certified-real names allow terminating outward interval refinement to obtain an integer \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}\ge Q_{\star}\).  The search for \(m_{\star}\), enumeration of the finite translated-dyadic grid, and all subsequent arithmetic are finite.  Since \(a_{\mathrm{an}}>0\), interval refinement also terminates with a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\le a_{\mathrm{an}}\).  These operations use only the displayed primitive constants and never the unknown transform or law of \(\eta\).  Equations (1)--(4) are uniform in \(n\), so the same computed bank and certificate work for every represented transform.
statements.justification: The translated-dyadic search and Blaschke--Harnack bound compute one uniformly conditioned bank from certified-real primitive constants without the unknown noise law.
statements.gap: Its certificate deteriorates with the fixed separation constants and does not resolve shrinking separation.
statements.consumer: The certified selector uses the bank and dyadic modulus in every stopping rule.

statements.statement:
If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), then it contains a one-dimensional submodel \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) with the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0,q_0,\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), independent Gaussian outcome innovation of fixed positive variance not exceeding the \(\psi_{\xi}\) envelope, and \(Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}\). For \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})\le C_0h^2\), where \(c_0,C_0\) depend only on fixed class constants. Moreover, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\), the same construction may be started from any \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and preserves its law of \((X,T)\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\), the noise \(\eta\), both clipped supplied codes, and therefore the two bounds
\[
 \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
 \qquad
 \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]
Every law on this second path belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), has target \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\), and obeys the same product relative-entropy bound. Consequently there is \(c_{\mathrm{ACE}}>0\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \ge \frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix
\[
 \tau=\frac{\psi_{\xi}}4>0,
 \qquad
 c_0=\min\{C_{\theta},1\}>0,
\]
and let \(\xi_{\star}\sim N(0,\tau^2)\) be independent of \((X,T)\). For the exact Luxemburg convention, if \(W\sim N(0,\tau^2)\), then
\[
 E\exp(W^2/u^2)=(1-2\tau^2/u^2)^{-1/2}
 \quad\text{for }u^2>2\tau^2.
\]
It follows that \(\|W\|_{\psi_2}=\sqrt{8/3}\,\tau<\psi_{\xi}\). Thus the chosen innovation has fixed positive variance and satisfies the required conditional sub-Gaussian envelope when conditioned on any \(X\).

First suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and fix \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\). Preserve its joint law of \((X,T)\), hence its \(g_0\), \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\), covariate law, deterministic clipped codes, and code errors. Preserve also its function \(q_0\), and, for \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), define
\[
 Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Since \(\eta\perp X\) and \(E\eta=0\),
\[
 E[Y_{\vartheta}\mid X]=q_0(X).
\]
The residual innovation under coefficient \(\vartheta\) is exactly \(\xi_{\star}\), and independence gives
\[
 E[\xi_{\star}\mid X,T]=0.
\]
The target range holds because \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\le C_{\theta}\). The bounds on \(g_0\) and \(q_0\), independence and sub-Gaussianity of \(\eta\), its cumulant separation, and the direct \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code bound are unchanged. The displayed Gaussian calculation gives the conditional sub-Gaussian bound for the new outcome innovation. Hence every law \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) defined by (1) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), and all objects asserted to be common along the path are indeed common.

Conditional on \((X,T)\), two path laws differ only in the means of normal distributions with common variance \(\tau^2\). Therefore
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1})
 =\frac{(\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)^2}{2\tau^2}E[(T-g_0(X))^2]
 =\frac{(\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)^2}{2\tau^2}E[\eta^2].
 \tag{2}
\]
The exact treatment-noise Luxemburg condition and Jensen's inequality imply
\[
 \exp\{E\eta^2/\psi_{\eta}^2\}
 \le E\exp(\eta^2/\psi_{\eta}^2)\le2,
 \qquad
 E\eta^2\le\psi_{\eta}^2\log2.
 \tag{3}
\]
Additivity of relative entropy for independent products, (2), and (3) show that whenever \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})
 \le C_0h^2,
 \qquad
 C_0=\frac{\psi_{\eta}^2\log2}{2\tau^2}.
 \tag{4}
\]
This proves the first branch with constants depending only on the fixed class constants.

Now suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\) and fix an arbitrary \(P^{\circ}\) in that class. Repeat (1), preserving the joint law of \((X,T)\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\), the treatment noise \(\eta\), and the deterministic functions \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\). We verify every condition in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\). The restrictions on \(g_0\) and \(q_0\) are unchanged. All treatment-side properties are unchanged: \(\eta\perp X\), \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\), and \(|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta\). Because neither regression function nor either clipped code changes,
\[
 \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
 \qquad
 \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}
\]
remain exactly the original two inequalities. The new coefficient obeys \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\le C_{\theta}\). The new residual is \(\xi_{\star}\), so the calculation above gives \(\|\xi_{\star}\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and independence gives \(E[\xi_{\star}\mid X,T]=0\). Finally, the size-\(n\) experiment is the independent product \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\otimes n}\), exactly as required by \(\text{ass:iid-sampling}\). Thus every law on the second path belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), and (2)--(4) apply without change.

It remains to turn this path into the asserted ACE-class converse. Choose
\[
 0<h\le\min\{c_0,1,(8C_0)^{-1/2}\},
 \qquad
 \vartheta_{\pm}=\pm\frac{h}{2\sqrt n}.
\]
For every \(n\ge2\), both values lie in the path, their separation is \(h/\sqrt n\), and (4) gives product relative entropy at most \(1/8\). Pinsker's inequality, which follows from the binary log-sum bound, gives
\[
 \|P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}-P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\sqrt{\frac12D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n})}
 \le\frac14.
 \tag{5}
\]
For an arbitrary estimator \(\widetilde\theta\), put \(A=\{\widetilde\theta\ge0\}\). On \(A\) under the negative law, or on \(A^c\) under the positive law, the squared error is at least \(h^2/(4n)\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \max_{v\in\{-,+\}}
 E_{P_{n,\vartheta_v}}[(\widetilde\theta-\vartheta_v)^2]
 &\ge \frac{h^2}{8n}
 \{P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}(A)
   +P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n}(A^c)\}\\
 &\ge \frac{h^2}{8n}
 \{1-\|P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}-P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}\\
 &\ge\frac{3h^2}{32n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Both laws belong to the published ACE class. Taking the supremum over that class and then the infimum over all sample estimators proves the final display with \(c_{\mathrm{ACE}}=3h^2/32>0\).

Fix once for all the actual positive primitive-name record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and the actual represented range record \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\). Under this shared-record convention, \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) specify once for all a deterministic translated-dyadic bank and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\) from the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\). There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total Borel statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), whose ordinary-sample interpretation uses those same fixed primitive records and canonicalizes only observation coordinates, satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). If a concrete implementation satisfying \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\) is added and compiled, then, relative to the canonical floor-dyadic observation records and exactly the same fixed records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\), the statistic is also the value of a total executable represented-data transducer returning a certified-real name. The correspondence claim does not quantify over alternative primitive records. Identical full input records, including their primitive components, give identical traces and output records; no Type-2 computability or trace extensionality across arbitrary alternative real names is asserted. Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\). Hence, whenever \(n\ge2\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
 \frac cn
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted. The finite-order ACE and spectral generalized-quantile guarantees may therefore be compared on the full published ACE class, and that class itself has matched \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) minimax mean-squared error. The latter lower bound is over all estimators on the class; it is not a lower bound on \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) or on its cited generalized-quantile guarantee. The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) remains the additional \(L^s(P_X)\)-restricted subclass and equals the published ACE class when \(s=r\) under the common clipped-code convention. The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, uniform inference result, or matching local lower bound.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the shared-record representation claim, the uniform upper bound, the two minimax converses, and the quantile and comparator conclusions.

\emph{1. Mathematical and represented-data layers.}  Fix the exact records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) from \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\).  They are selected once before \(P\), \(n\), the observation records, and the execution trace vary.  Unfold \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\).  The real interval formulas are sound because the extrema of a bilinear function on a rectangle occur at its corners.  Substitution into
\[
 (x+iy)(u+iv)=(xu-yv)+i(xv+yu)
\]
proves complex multiplication containment.  The square lower and upper formulas enclose each coordinate square, rational square-root bisection preserves its bracketing invariant, and a positive lower modulus certificate makes \(u^2+v^2\) strictly positive.  The displayed conjugate formula and outward division therefore prove guarded complex-division containment.

Machin's identity and the alternating remainder prove the certified \(\pi\) contract with the displayed finite cutoff.  On a bounded input interval, the Lagrange remainder bounds and the explicit cutoff in the definition prove the real exponential, sine, and cosine contracts.  Hence
\[
 e^{x+iy}=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)
\]
proves the complex-exponential rectangle contract.  Finite induction proves the sum and product contracts.  On every mesh cell, a function with Lipschitz constant \(L\) differs from its node value by at most \(L/N_{\mathrm{mesh}}\); integration and taking finite endpoint minima prove the quadrature and boundary-infimum contracts.  Every cutoff is an explicit integer formula and every operation is finite.

Consequently, if a concrete module implementing these algorithms and contracts is added and compiled, the represented-data procedure in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), on the full records whose primitive components are exactly \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\), is a total transducer.  Its output is a certified-real record because the final clipping formula
\[
 \frac{|y+C_{\theta}|-|y-C_{\theta}|}{2}
\]
is a composition of implemented certified operations and equals \(\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}(y)\) by the three cases \(y<-C_{\theta}\), \(|y|\le C_{\theta}\), and \(y>C_{\theta}\).  No undecidable comparison is used.  Identical full input records, including these same fixed primitive components, make the same finite modulus calls and rational comparisons, hence have identical traces and output records.  This conditional represented-data conclusion neither quantifies over alternative primitive records nor asserts extensionality across arbitrary alternative names.

Independently of compilation, the ordinary-sample interpretation uses those same fixed primitive records and canonicalizes only the observation coordinates.  For a fixed terminal trace, every queried observation endpoint is a floor of a scaled sample coordinate and is therefore Borel measurable.  Rational arithmetic and rational endpoint comparisons preserve Borel measurability.  The set of finite traces is countable, so partitioning the sample space by terminal trace proves that \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) is a total Borel statistic.  By definition of the two layers, the value returned by the transducer on the full fixed-record input equals this Borel statistic.  Inspection shows that it uses \(\bar g_n\), no supplied outcome code, and no treatment-noise law.

\emph{2. Uniform upper bound.}  Fix \(n\ge2\), \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\).  Let \(j_{\star}\) be supplied by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).  By \(\text{lem:l1-nuisance-zero-free}\),
\[
 N_{C_{j_{\star}}}(F_n)\ge1,
 \qquad
 \inf_{C_{j_{\star}}}|F_n|\ge\frac{3a_{\star}}4. \tag{1}
\]
For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), put
\[
 d_a=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|,
 \quad
 e_a=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|,
 \quad
 \mathcal A_a=\{d_a\le a_{\star}/8\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_0\), soundness and the width \(a_{\star}/64\) of the certified modulus interval give the candidate \(j_{\star}\) a lower endpoint at least
\[
 \left(\frac34-\frac18-\frac1{64}\right)a_{\star}
 =\frac{39a_{\star}}{64}. \tag{2}
\]
The straight-line homotopy between \(F_n\) and \(\widehat F_{0,n}\) is nonzero on this circle, so their winding numbers agree and are positive.  Thus \(j_{\star}\) is admissible.

Let \(C=C_{\widehat j_n}\).  Maximality of the selected rational lower endpoint, (2), and subtraction of \(d_0\) give
\[
 \inf_C|F_n|\ge\frac{31a_{\star}}{64}. \tag{3}
\]
The same homotopy and the sound winding enclosure give
\[
 \widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}=N_C(F_n)=:N\ge1. \tag{4}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_0\cap\mathcal A_1\), the evaluation empirical modulus is at least \(23a_{\star}/64\); after the enclosure width is subtracted, its lower endpoint exceeds \(a_{\star}/4\).  Hence the evaluation branch does not fall back.

There is a constant \(C_G<\infty\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},R_1\), such that
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R_1}|G_n(z)|\le C_G. \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\), and \(Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta+\xi\).  The exact Luxemburg inequalities and Young's inequality give
\[
 E_Pe^{t|\eta|}\le\sqrt2e^{t^2\psi_{\eta}^2/2},
\]
and the same convention bounds the second moments of \(\eta\) and \(\xi\).  Cauchy--Schwarz then bounds \(E_P[|Y|e^{R_1|Z_n|}]\), proving (5) without independence between \(\xi\) and \(\eta\).

Subtract the empirical and population ratios on \(C\).  From (3)--(5), \(\operatorname{len}(C)\le2\pi R_1\), and \(N\ge1\),
\[
 \left|
 \frac1{N2\pi i}\oint_C\frac{\widehat G_{1,n}}{\widehat F_{1,n}}\,dz
 -\frac1{N2\pi i}\oint_C\frac{G_n}{F_n}\,dz
 \right|
 \le L_{\mathrm{rat}}(d_1+e_1), \tag{6}
\]
where, with \(\mu=31a_{\star}/64\) and \(\nu=23a_{\star}/64\), one may take
\[
 L_{\mathrm{rat}}=R_1\max\{\nu^{-1},C_G(\mu\nu)^{-1}\}. \tag{7}
\]
The hypotheses of \(\text{thm:exact-contour-identification}\) hold: (3) makes \(F_n\) zero-free on \(C\), \(\text{lem:l1-nuisance-zero-free}\) makes \(H_n\) zero-free on and inside \(C\), and (4) supplies a positive count.  Hence the population contour in (6) equals the causal target \(\theta_0(P)\).  The final rational midpoint adds at most \(1/n\), and real part followed by projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) cannot increase distance from \(\theta_0(P)\).

Both fold sizes are at least \(n/3\).  Therefore \(\text{lem:empirical-transform-uniform-l2}\) and Markov's inequality give, for its constant \(K\),
\[
 E_P(d_a^2+e_a^2)\le\frac{3K}{n},
 \qquad
 P(\mathcal A_0^c\cup\mathcal A_1^c)
 \le\frac{384K}{a_{\star}^2n}. \tag{8}
\]
Projection bounds squared error by \(4C_{\theta}^2\) on the exceptional event.  On the good event, (6), \((d_1+e_1)^2\le2(d_1^2+e_1^2)\), and the numerical error give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{n}, \tag{9}
\]
with, for example,
\[
 C_{\mathrm{up}}
 =12L_{\mathrm{rat}}^2K
 +\frac{1536C_{\theta}^2K}{a_{\star}^2}+2. \tag{10}
\]
The bank, \(a_{\star}\), \(C_G\), \(K\), and \(L_{\mathrm{rat}}\) depend only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\).  A width-one refinement of the fixed valid primitive record has an upper endpoint at most its represented value plus one.  Thus \(C_{\mathrm{up}}\) is selected outside all quantifiers over \(P\), \(n\), represented observation records, traces, and laws, and it is independent of \(\gamma\).  Since the Borel statistic is one data-driven rule, (9) proves the minimax upper bound.

\emph{3. Converses and quantiles.}  Apply the first branch of \(\text{lem:non-gaussian-hard-submodel}\).  Choose fixed \(h>0\), depending only on class constants, such that \(\vartheta_{\pm}=\pm h/(2\sqrt n)\) lie on its path and the product relative entropy is at most \(1/8\).  Pinsker's inequality gives total variation at most \(1/4\).  Testing by the sign of an arbitrary estimator yields
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-,+\}}
 E_{P_{n,\vartheta_v}}[(\widetilde\theta-\vartheta_v)^2]
 \ge\frac{h^2}{8n}(1-1/4)
 =\frac{3h^2}{32n}. \tag{11}
\]
Thus \(c_{\mathrm{NG}}/n\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\).

By \(\text{lem:jms-ace-class-relations}\),
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}. \tag{12}
\]
Restriction of (9) proves the spectral upper bound on the full published ACE class.  The second branch of \(\text{lem:non-gaussian-hard-submodel}\) gives on this same class
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \ge\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}. \tag{13}
\]
The Borel statistic is admissible in this infimum.  Taking
\[
 c=\min\{c_{\mathrm{NG}},c_{\mathrm{ACE}}\}>0,
 \qquad C=C_{\mathrm{up}}
\]
proves both MSE brackets.

Finally, (9) and Markov's inequality give
\[
 P\left(
 |\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|
 >\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}
 \right)\le\gamma,
\]
 which is the stated generalized-quantile bound; (12) gives its ACE-class restriction.  The class-relation lemma also proves the \(L^s(P_X)\) subclass statement and equality at \(s=r\), but no reverse inclusion for the broad spectral class.  The constant \(C_{\gamma}\) belongs only to the cited ACE theorem: for fixed \(\gamma\) it is chosen outside all \(P,n\) quantifiers, is not an algorithm input, and does not enter (9)--(10).  The lower bound (13) is over all estimators, not the ACE estimator.  Every constant may deteriorate as fixed \(\delta\) decreases; no shrinking-separation rate, adaptive switch, uniform inference result, or local converse has been proved.
statements.justification: The total certified statistic attains a matched parametric MSE rate for the scalar causal coefficient without an outcome learner or knowledge of the treatment-noise law.
statements.gap: The constants are fixed-separation constants and do not yield a useful shrinking-separation rate or uniform inference theorem.
statements.consumer: Use as the effective fixed-separation estimation theorem and retain all stated scope disclaimers.

statements.proof_tex:
The three class relations are exactly \(\text{lem:jms-ace-class-relations}\).  In particular, the first inclusion is maximal in the direction needed here: every published ACE law is a member of the broad spectral class, whereas no reverse inclusion is used or claimed.

Assume \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\).  If \(\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), the cited result \(\text{lem:jms-ace-quantile-upper}\) applies directly on the full class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and gives exactly
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}. \tag{1}
\]

Suppose instead that \(\varepsilon_{2,n}=0\).  For \(t\in(0,\varepsilon_{1,n})\), enlarge only the outcome-code radius from zero to \(t\).  Every law in the zero-radius class remains in the radius-\(t\) class.  Moreover,
\[
 \max\!\left\{\varepsilon_{1,n},t,
  (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\right\}
 =
 \max\!\left\{\varepsilon_{1,n},0,
  (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\right\}.
\]
Thus \(b_{2,n}\), and hence the eligibility predicate, is unchanged.  Apply the positive-radius cited theorem with radius \(t\), then restrict its supremum to the zero-radius class.  The resulting right-hand side differs from the claimed boundary value only by
\[
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}\varepsilon_{1,n}^rt.
\]
The published statistic is the same order-\(r\) ACE statistic for every radius.  Letting \(t\downarrow0\) proves (1) at the boundary.

Now also assume \(n\ge2\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\).  By \(\text{lem:jms-ace-class-relations}\), this class is contained in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), so the latter is nonempty.  Restricting the generalized-quantile inequality in the proposed form of \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) to the subset gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}. \tag{2}
\]

Finally put
\[
 S_n=\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
     +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}.
\]
All multiplicative quantities in \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\) other than \(S_n\) and \(n^{-1/2}\) are fixed positive class constants.  Along any eligible sequence for which \(S_n\gg n^{-1/2}\), (1) is therefore of order \(S_n\), while (2) is of order \(n^{-1/2}\).  Their ratio tends to zero.  This proves a strict comparison of the two displayed upper guarantees on the full published ACE class and, because no risk lower bound for the ACE statistic was used, proves the final caveat.
statements.justification: Probability-space norm monotonicity proves the comparison-class inclusion under exactly \(s\ge r\), after which the published theorem applies, including the zero outcome-radius boundary extension.
statements.gap: The broad spectral class does not impose the outcome-code or higher-norm conditions needed for the published ACE class.
statements.consumer: Apply the cited generalized-quantile upper bound directly on the full published ACE class and compare it there with the transported spectral upper guarantee. The comparison remains upper-versus-upper and gives no lower bound for the ACE estimator; the auxiliary \(L^s\) subclass only records the stronger-code comparison and equality at \(s=r\).

The following are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes. Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. Also fix once for all the exact primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) specified in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\). Under this shared-record convention, apply and fix the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank and positive dyadic certificate specified by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\). Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\). The witnessing total Borel statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Its ordinary-sample interpretation canonicalizes only observation-coordinate records and uses the same fixed primitive records. If the bounded-build substrate in \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\) is concretely implemented and compiled, the statistic is additionally delivered by the represented-data transducer on the identical fixed primitive records and supplied canonical observation records. Its correspondence claim does not quantify over alternative primitive records, and trace determinism is asserted only for identical full input records. No computability claim from arbitrary alternative real names is made. Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection of \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\). Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) is solely a diagnostic of the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2; its positive lower-bound claim is not used. These conclusions neither form a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy nor determine a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
Apply the proposed form of \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) under the fixed shared records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\).  Its bank is specified once from \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) by \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\), without the treatment-noise law.  Along every displayed eligible sequence it gives constants independent of \(n\) such that
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le\frac Cn.
\]
Hence \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}\).  Only \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\) is required, so fixed nonzero eligible treatment-code radii are included.

The construction of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) imposes the direct \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code restriction and no condition involving \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\).  The Borel statistic in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) likewise uses \(T_i,Y_i,\bar g_n(X_i)\), but no supplied outcome code.  Its mathematical layer uses the fixed primitive records and canonicalizes only these observation coordinates.  If the bounded-build arithmetic substrate is implemented and compiled, the representation conclusion of the proposed minimax theorem supplies the additional transducer on exactly the same fixed primitive records.  The correspondence claim does not range over alternative primitive records, and identical traces are asserted only for identical full input records.

Separately, \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) proves that every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) has \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  If this class is nonempty, the identically zero statistic has zero squared error and zero absolute-error generalized quantile under every member.  Nonnegativity of the two losses in \(\text{def:minimax-risks}\) therefore gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=0.
\]
This calculation uses only the simultaneous exact conditional-mean restriction, bounded observed outcome, and nondegenerate Gaussian treatment noise; it does not use a positive lower-bound assertion from the cited source.

Finally, the classes are separate.  Indeed, \(k=r+1\ge3\); Gaussian treatment noise has zero cumulants of all orders at least three, whereas every law in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) has \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta>0\).  Thus, when both classes are nonempty, they are disjoint and therefore incomparable.  The two displays neither compare a common local experiment nor determine a shrinking-separation frontier.  This proves all scope qualifications.
statements.justification: The theorem records the fixed-separated non-Gaussian rate and the Gaussian zero-target diagnostic as separate facts on separately defined classes.
statements.gap: The incomparable classes do not determine a local-to-Gaussian frontier.
statements.consumer: Do not describe the paired display as a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy.

For every \(n\) such that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi\), let \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\). Suppose that \(\eta\sim\tfrac12N(-1,1)+\tfrac12N(1,1)\), \(\eta\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Then \(\kappa_4(\eta)=-2\), \(M(i\pi/2)=0\), and
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)\right]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P\!\left[\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)\right]
\ge \frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that, uniformly over all laws \(P\) satisfying the preceding conditions,
\[
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]\le \frac{C}{n}.
\]
No condition on the supplied outcome code or on \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) is required.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(a=\pi/2\). Represent the stipulated mixture as \(\eta=R+E\), where \(R\) is symmetric Rademacher, \(E\sim N(0,1)\), and \(R\perp E\). Then
\[
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}]=e^{z^2/2}\cosh z,
\qquad
M(ia)=e^{-a^2/2}\cos a=0.
\]
Moreover, \(E_P[\eta]=0\), \(E_P[\eta^2]=2\), and independence gives
\[
E_P[\eta^4]
=E_P[R^4]+6E_P[R^2]E_P[E^2]+E_P[E^4]
=1+6+3=10.
\]
The centered fourth-cumulant identity therefore yields
\[
\kappa_4(\eta)=E_P[\eta^4]-3E_P[\eta^2]^2=10-3\cdot2^2=-2.
\]

The characteristic function of \(\eta\) is
\[
\phi(t)=E_P[e^{it\eta}]=e^{-t^2/2}\cos t.
\]
For any deterministic \(d\in\mathbb R\), symmetry of \(\eta\) gives
\[
E_P[\cos\{t(\eta+d)\}]=\phi(t)\cos(td).
\]
Differentiation under the expectation is valid because the Gaussian mixture has a finite first moment. Hence
\[
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{t(\eta+d)\}]
=-\frac{d}{dt}\{\phi(t)\cos(td)\}.
\]
Since \(\phi(a)=0\) and \(\phi'(a)=-e^{-a^2/2}\), evaluation at \(a=\pi/2\) gives
\[
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=e^{-a^2/2}\cos(ad).
\]
The variable \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), so \(\eta\perp X\) implies \(\eta\perp D_n\). Conditioning on \(D_n\) and using \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\),
\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(aZ_n)]
=e^{-a^2/2}E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P[\cos(\pi D_n/2)].
\]
The direct \(L^1(P_X)\) premise is exactly
\[
E_P|D_n|=\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
Using \(1-\cos u\le |u|\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/\pi\),
\[
E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
\ge1-aE_P|D_n|
\ge1-\frac{\pi}{2}\frac1\pi
=\frac12.
\]
Thus
\[
c_0:=\frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}>0
\]
is a uniform population relevance and division bound. The cutoff in \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}\) prevents division below \(c_0/2\).

For the risk calculation define
\[
W_i:=Z_{n,i}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\qquad
V_i:=\{Y_i-\theta_0(P)Z_{n,i}\}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\]
and let \(\bar W_n=\mathbb P_nW\) and \(\bar V_n=\mathbb P_nV\). The residual identity is
\[
Y-\theta_0(P)Z_n=b_n(X)+\xi,
\qquad
b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0(P)D_n.
\]
For every \(d\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P[\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=\operatorname{Im}\{e^{iad}\phi(a)\}=0.
\]
Consequently, conditioning on \(X\) gives
\[
E_P[b_n(X)\sin(aZ_n)]=0.
\]
Because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), the conditional-mean restriction gives
\[
E_P[\xi\sin(aZ_n)]
=E_P\!\left[E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\sin(aZ_n)\right]=0.
\]
Therefore \(E_P[V_i]=0\).

The clipping definition and the range restriction imply \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely. Set
\[
b_{\max}:=C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g.
\]
Then \(|b_n(X)|\le b_{\max}\). The conditional sub-Gaussian condition entails \(E_P[\xi^2]\le K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2\) for a finite universal constant \(K_{\xi}\) determined only by the convention for the conditional \(\psi_2\)-norm. Since \(|\sin u|\le1\),
\[
E_P[V_i^2]
\le2b_{\max}^2+2K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2
=:K_V.
\]
Also, \(E_P[\eta^2]=2\), \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), and \(|\sin u|\le1\) imply
\[
E_P[W_i^2]
\le E_P[Z_n^2]
\le2E_P[\eta^2]+2E_P[D_n^2]
\le4+8C_g^2
=:K_W.
\]
These bounds verify the integrability needed for conditioning, differentiation, and the variance calculations.

Let \(\mathcal A_n=\{\bar W_n\ge c_0/2\}\), the event on which the sample ratio is used. Projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) cannot increase distance from \(\theta_0(P)\). Thus, on \(\mathcal A_n\),
\[
|\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P)|^2
\le\frac{\bar V_n^2}{\bar W_n^2}
\le\frac{4\bar V_n^2}{c_0^2}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_n^c\), clipping bounds the squared loss by \(4C_{\theta}^2\). If \(m_W=E_P[W_i]\), then \(m_W\ge c_0\). Independent and identically distributed sampling and Chebyshev's inequality therefore give
\[
P(\mathcal A_n^c)
\le P\!\left(|\bar W_n-m_W|\ge\frac{c_0}{2}\right)
\le\frac{4\operatorname{Var}_P(W_i)}{nc_0^2}
\le\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}.
\]
The same sampling condition and \(E_P[V_i]=0\) yield
\[
E_P[\bar V_n^2]
=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_P(V_i)}{n}
\le\frac{K_V}{n}.
\]
Combining the two events,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
&\le\frac{4K_V}{nc_0^2}
+4C_{\theta}^2\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}\\
&=\frac{4K_V+16C_{\theta}^2K_W}{c_0^2}\,\frac1n.
\end{aligned}
\]
The constant depends only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), and not on \(P\), \(n\), the supplied outcome code, or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). This proves the proposition, including its support, relevance, positivity, integrability, and fallback boundary conditions.

\]
whenever \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\); the executable represented-data conclusion is conditional on implementing and compiling \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\).  n^{-1}\Delta_a^{-1/2}

 \right\}
\]
provided \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\Delta_a^{1/4}/(2^{1/4}\pi)\). These results do not define or attain a sharp full-class shrinking-separation rate, construct an adaptive selector or confidence procedure, or furnish a matching local lower bound.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), the externally supplied deterministic code pair is fixed before \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\) is drawn. The spectral algorithm receives canonical dyadic names of \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\), internally computes the bank from canonical certified names of \(k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1\), and derives every empirical transform, derivative, Lipschitz, winding, and final-integrand enclosure by finite outward rational refinement. It receives neither an externally selected bank nor the treatment-noise law.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment with \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\). The fixed-separated spectral class imposes independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian treatment noise. The separate Gaussian intersection reproduces simultaneous known-variance and bounded-observed-outcome assumptions used only for the source-assumption diagnostic.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used. Spectral relevance is expressed by a positive winding number and a contour boundary modulus bounded away from zero; the Gaussian degeneracy proof uses bounded outcome support and nondegenerate Gaussian support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The deterministic radii \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) are nonincreasing. The broad spectral class and estimator require only sufficiently small direct \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code error and impose no supplied outcome-code restriction. The full published ACE class has stronger \(L^r(P_X)\) treatment- and outcome-code restrictions and is therefore contained in the broad spectral class. The auxiliary class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) adds both \(L^s(P_X)\) restrictions; it is a subclass for \(s\ge r\) and equals the published ACE class at \(s=r\).

estimand_functional: Fix once for all the actual positive primitive-name record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) for \((\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\) and the represented range record \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\). Relative to these same fixed records, the certified translated-dyadic bank and the ordinary-sample Borel statistic define an observed-sample map that canonicalizes only observation coordinates and satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]\le C/n\). If the bounded-build substrate is concretely implemented and compiled, the represented-data transducer on those identical fixed primitive records returns a certified-real name with the same value; no correspondence over alternative primitive records is claimed.

tldr: For fixed nonzero cumulant separation, a once-for-all certified translated-dyadic contour bank and a total split-sample statistic identify and estimate the partially linear causal coefficient with uniform matched \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) mean-squared error using only a sufficiently accurate direct \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment code, no outcome learner, and no knowledge of the treatment-noise law. An ACE-preserving outcome-tilt converse and the spectral upper bound give the same matched minimax order on the full published ACE class, while the cited ACE-versus-spectral generalized-quantile comparison remains strictly upper-versus-upper. The bounded-outcome Gaussian calculation is only a source-assumption diagnostic: the simultaneous stated restrictions force \(\theta_0=0\).

project_justification.gap: Finite-order orthogonal and ACE methods provide nuisance-dependent upper guarantees, while classical location-family work recognizes transform zeros; neither supplies the present learned-residual contour estimator with an explicit certified translated-dyadic bank and matched fixed-separation minimax MSE. The published ACE class does embed in the broad direct-\(L^1(P_X)\) spectral class, which licenses a full-class upper-guarantee comparison but not an ACE lower bound. The simultaneous bounded-outcome Gaussian assumptions around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2 instead force the target to vanish and therefore serve only as a source-assumption diagnostic.
project_justification.niche: Independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian treatment noise creates an exact null space for every location shift induced by treatment-code error. A sufficiently small fixed direct \(L^1(P_X)\) residual contamination preserves observable zero geometry, while certified-real primitive constants suffice to compute a uniformly conditioned contour bank without the unknown noise law. Because an \(L^r(P_X)\) treatment-code guarantee implies this \(L^1(P_X)\) condition, the construction applies throughout the full published ACE comparison class.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves exact annihilator and observable contour identities, the numerical zero radius, a terminating certified translated-dyadic bank construction with a positive dyadic modulus, empirical-transform control, a total certified statistic, and matching \(c/n\) and \(C/n\) MSE bounds on the broad spectral class. By preserving both published \(L^r(P_X)\) code restrictions in the outcome-tilt submodel, it also proves matching class-minimax MSE bounds on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\). It retains Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 5.4 only as an estimator-specific generalized-quantile upper comparator and treats the bounded-outcome Gaussian calculation solely as a separate source-assumption diagnostic.

interpretation: The causal target is \(\theta_0(P)\); the observable contour ratio is its identifying functional only on contours satisfying the proved zero-free and positive-count conditions. At fixed separation, certification turns that identity into a computable sample statistic with matched parametric MSE on the broad direct-\(L^1(P_X)\) class. Because the lower-bound outcome tilt also preserves both published \(L^r(P_X)\) code restrictions, the full published ACE class has the same matched minimax MSE order. This is a class-level statement over all estimators, not a lower bound for the particular ACE statistic or its generalized-quantile upper guarantee. The Gaussian bounded-outcome proposition does not establish a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy: it shows only that one simultaneous source-stated intersection has the identically zero target.
technical_internal_limitation: Constants in the contour-bank and risk bounds may deteriorate as \(\delta\downarrow0\). The ACE comparison is an upper-guarantee comparison, not a lower bound for ACE.
